text:
maya: Heads up — we've been seeing sporadic packet loss on the overlay between gpu nodes in eu-west-1b since ~08:10. Affected pods are mostly long-lived GPU inference workers, manifests as increased E2E latency and occasional model RPC timeouts.

jon: How frequent? single node or multiple?

maya: ~every 5-10m a burst of packet drops for ~10-30s. At least 3 nodes show it (gpu-1,gpu-4,gpu-5). Not all pods on the node fail, just flows going to other nodes.

kevin: Any recent platform changes? kernel / driver updates, cni upgrades, or cloud patching?

maya: We rolled a minor Cilium config change yesterday (enableBPFMasquerade=true) but that was low-risk. No kernel bumps.

laura: Can you paste output of `ip link` and `ethtool -k` from one affected node?

maya: Pasting trimmed outputs:
```
$ ip link show vxlan0
4: vxlan0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether 0a:58:3d:xx:xx:xx brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
$ ethtool -k eth0 | sed -n '1,18p'
rx-checksumming: on\ntx-checksumming: on\nscatter-gather: on\n	gso: on\n	rsc: off\n	lro: off
```

kevin: MTU 1500 on vxlan? overlay encapsulation will add ~50 bytes. Could be fragmentation or drops if underlying path enforces a smaller MTU. Do we use jumbo frames anywhere?

maya: Underlying iface is 9000 on the host, but I see Cilium's tunnel interface set to 1500. Not sure about intermediate path MTU.

jon: Can you run a quick pingsize test between two affected nodes: `ping -M do -s 1400 <peer>` and increase until failure? Also tcpdump for VXLAN UDP packets on host, e.g., `tcpdump -n -i eth0 udp and port 4789` (or 8472 for geneve).

maya: Ran ping: max without fragmentation ~1430. At 1440 it starts fragmentation when DF=1. tcpdump shows bursts of no responses during incidents. Sample: `17:02:41.123456 IP hostA > hostB: UDP, length 1508` and then later you see `IP hostA > hostB: Message too long: mtu 1432` in dmesg.

kevin: That suggests an MTU path issue — VXLAN encaps pushes size > MTU causing drops. Why underlying mtu=9000 but path reports smaller? Could be an intermediate virtual switch (cloud hypervisor) or host NIC offload incorrectly reporting.

laura: Also check offloads (GRO/TSO/LRO) — sometimes they mask MTU problems; disabling them can make it reproducible. `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off` then retest.

maya: Did that, and when disabling GRO+TSO the error frequency drops but doesn't vanish. After disabling offloads the drops are rarer.

jon: Are we using SR-IOV or any accelerated path on these instances? Also any ENI trunking? That could change perceived MTU.

maya: Instances are ml.gpu.large with ENA. No SR-IOV configured.

kevin: Another angle: Cilium's masquerade change might be causing larger packet sizes on host post-masq. If masqueraded packets get encapsulated and then masqueraded again, you'd blow MTU. Check iptables POSTROUTING rules on node when it's happening.

maya: I captured `iptables -t nat -S POSTROUTING` and it's pretty standard. No double-masq rules.

laura: Any signs in cloud provider NIC logs? Maybe hypervisor does conservative MTU on some hosts due to offload bug. Check `dmesg | grep -i mtu` and provider-specific agent logs.

maya: dmesg has repeated lines during event: `NETDEV WATCHDOG: eth0 (ena): transmit queue 0 timed out` and `excessive gso/tx completion delayed` around same timestamps.

kevin: Queue timeouts + GSO hints at driver/hardware stress. Could be the NIC firmware bug interacting with high packet rates from GPU RPCs. Are we saturating link? Check `sar -n DEV` and `ifstat` for that window.

maya: Link utilization spikes to ~70% during bursts, not full saturation. P95 packet rates high though.

jon: Quick mitigation: reduce MTU on vxlan to 1400 cluster-wide OR enable fragmentation-friendly settings. Also try lowering host MTU to 8950 -> not ideal. We should try vxlan mtu 1400 on one node via `ip link set dev vxlan0 mtu 1400` and schedule traffic through it.

maya: Did temporary change on gpu-4: `ip link set vxlan0 mtu 1400` — for ~30m no recurrence on that node while others still had issues.

laura: Good sign. Suggest we roll vxlan mtu 1400 via a daemonset patch in cilium-tunnel config and monitor for 24h.

kevin: Also file ticket with cloud NIC support — include dmesg snippets and ethtool -S counters. Might be firmware + offloads issue.

maya: Filing ticket now, attaching logs.

netops-bot: Incident created: NET-2145 — "Intermittent overlay packet drops (eu-west-1b)". Priority P2.

jon: Side note — for RDMA paths (in our infra we have ib0 but not used for cross-node RPCs here) confirm none of these GPU pods accidentally bind to IB interface; that could cause weird route selection.

maya: Confirmed: pods bind to eth0/vxlan paths only. No IB involvement.

laura: Plan: 1) roll vxlan mtu 1400 via cilium config canary on eu-west-1b (start with 20% nodes) 2) open cloud NIC FW ticket 3) monitor p99 latency + packet drops 4) consider offload toggle as emergency rollback.

kevin: Agreed. If canary looks good, we keep mtu change cluster-wide for now — better than opaque packet loss.

maya: Starting canary now (20% of gpu nodes). Will update thread with metrics after 1 hour. Thanks. :thumbsup:
